src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
s: What is the name of the confidential documents that were leaked in November, 2017 revealing names of several Indians having offshore investments?
x: The Paradise Papers (November 2017, ICIJ) were leaked records of offshore law firm Appleby naming several Indians with offshore investments. The Panama Papers were the 2016 leak.

s: On which subject was the Santhanam Committee constituted?
x: The Santhanam Committee was the Committee on Prevention of Corruption; the CBI followed in 1963 and the CVC in 1964.

s: When did the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 come into force?
x: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act came into force on 1 July 2005.

s: In which year did India ratify the United Nations Convention against Corruption?
x: The Convention was adopted in 2003, India signed it in 2005 and ratified it in 2011.

s: The Enforcement Directorate functions primarily under which combination of laws?
o: RTI Act, 2005 and Official Secrets Act, 1923
x: The Enforcement Directorate operates under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, and the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.

s: The Santhanam Committee led to the setting up of which two bodies?
x: The Santhanam Committee (1962-64) led to the CBI in 1963 and the CVC in 1964.

s: In which year did India sign the UN Convention against Corruption?
x: UNCAC was adopted in 2003, signed by India in 2005 and ratified in 2011.

s: In August 2022 Supreme Court declared that Section 3(2) of the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act 1988 as unconstitutional. Section 3(2) of this act gives provision of the following punishment.
o: Three years maximum imprisonment or fine or both.
Properties held benami shall be subject to confiscation by Authority.
Maximum 5 years imprisonment and confiscation of properties.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act?
o: Bribe-giving became a direct offence punishable with up to seven years
It sought to align Indian law with the UN Convention against Corruption
Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf
A coerced bribe-giver is protected only if the matter is reported within 30 days
x: A coerced bribe-giver must report within 7 days, not 30.

s: Under the amended Prevention of Corruption Act, what imprisonment does a public servant convicted of taking a bribe face?
x: The amended Act prescribes three to seven years' imprisonment and a fine; trials should end within two years, extendable to four.

s: Before the CBI can investigate a case within a State's territory, it needs the consent of that State government under which provision?
o: Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Section 8 of the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003
x: The CBI draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946, and Section 6 of that Act requires the State's consent. Section 17A PCA is government approval before investigating a public servant's official decisions; Section 19 PCA is sanction before a court takes cognizance; the CVC Act is about the CVC's superintendence, not State consent.

s: Under Section 2(c) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, which of the following does NOT correctly describe a 'public servant'?
o: An employee of a local authority
Only a permanent employee of the Union Government
A person whose office requires performance of a public duty
x: The definition covers local-authority employees, Judges and persons performing public duties; it is not limited to permanent Union employees.

s: Under the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act, within what time must a coerced bribe-giver report the matter to be protected?
x: A coerced bribe-giver is protected if he reports within 7 days, not 30.

s: Under the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018, trial must be completed within 2 years; up to what maximum period can it be extended?
x: The trial must finish within 2 years, extendable to a maximum of 4 years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018:
1. Bribe-giving was made a direct offence punishable with up to 7 years.
2. Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf.
3. Its purpose was to align the law with UNCAC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: bribe-giving became a direct offence (up to 7 years), commercial organisations became liable, and the aim was alignment with UNCAC.

src: APPSC Junior Accounts / Assistant Engineer in Municipalities
s: Indian Supreme Court upheld the right of a private citizen to seek sanction for prosecution of public servant for corruption on
In the split verdict on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, who struck it down as violating Article 14?
x: Justice Nagarathna struck Section 17A down under Article 14; Justice Viswanathan upheld it subject to a binding Lokpal or Lokayukta opinion.

s: Which section of the Prevention of Corruption Act requires prior sanction before a court takes cognizance of an offence?
x: Section 19 requires prior sanction before cognizance; Section 17A requires government approval before inquiry or investigation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sanction for prosecution of public servants?
o: Section 19 of the PC Act requires government approval before a police inquiry begins
Section 218 of the BNSS, corresponding to Section 197 CrPC, came into force on 1 July 2024
Since 2018, Section 19 sanction under the PC Act also covers retired public servants
Approval before an inquiry or investigation is governed by Section 17A of the PC Act
x: Prior approval before inquiry or investigation is Section 17A; Section 19 concerns sanction for prosecution.

s: Which Supreme Court judgments are cited as earlier precedents that struck down prior-sanction requirements for investigating public servants?
x: Vineet Narain (1997) and Subramanian Swamy (2014) struck down prior-sanction rules, the backdrop to the Section 17A challenge. Kesavananda and Minerva Mills concern the basic structure; Prakash Singh is police reform and Vishaka sexual harassment at the workplace; Lalita Kumari (mandatory FIR) and Arnesh Kumar (arrest guidelines) are not about prior sanction.

s: Which of the following pairs (provision – stage of protection) is correctly matched?
o: Sec 218 BNSS – General protection of public servants
x: Sec 218 BNSS (earlier Sec 197 CrPC) is the general protection; 17A is approval before investigation and 19 sanction before cognizance.

s: Before which of the following does Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act require government approval?
o: Inquiry or investigation into official decisions
Arrest of a retired public servant
x: Section 17A requires approval before inquiry or investigation; Section 19 requires sanction before a court takes cognizance.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in which year?
x: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in 2014. The reference to 2011 relates to the year in which the Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha.

s: Who among the following form the selection committee for the Director of the CBI?
o: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India or nominee, and Leader of Opposition
President, Vice-President and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Chief Ministers of all States
Chief Justice of India, Attorney General and Cabinet Secretary
x: The Director of the CBI is chosen by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India or the Chief Justice’s nominee, and the Leader of Opposition.

s: Who can be a whistleblower under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014?
o: only a Member of Parliament making a complaint to the Lokpal
only a government employee of the Union Government
a public servant or another person, including an NGO, making a public interest disclosure
x: A whistleblower includes any public servant or other person, including an NGO, who makes a public interest disclosure of specified wrongdoing to the Competent Authority.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the protection available under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014?
o: Acceptance of anonymous complaints as a general rule
Punishment for knowingly false or frivolous complaints
x: Anonymous complaints are not accepted as a general rule. The complainant’s identity is disclosed to the competent authority but is required to be kept confidential; protection against victimisation is also provided.

s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, which pair of person complained against and competent authority is correctly matched?
x: For Union Ministers the competent authority is the Prime Minister. Central employees go to the CVC, State Ministers to the CM, and MPs to the Rajya Sabha Chairman or Lok Sabha Speaker.

s: What is the punishment for a knowingly false complaint under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014?
x: A knowingly false complaint attracts up to 2 years and ₹30,000; revealing a complainant's identity attracts up to 3 years and ₹50,000.

s: Which of the following categories is specifically excluded from the stated whistleblower rules?
x: The Special Protection Group (SPG) is excluded from the stated rules.

s: With the dissolution of which Lok Sabha did the Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2015 lapse?
x: The Bill would have barred disclosures in Section 8(1)-type categories; it lapsed with the 16th Lok Sabha in 2019.

s: Within how many years must a complaint under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 be made?
x: Complaints must be made within 7 years, and anonymous complaints are not entertained.

s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, who is the competent authority for a complaint against a Union Minister?
x: Complaints against a Union Minister go to the Prime Minister; against a State Minister to the Chief Minister.

s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, what is the punishment for revealing the identity of a complainant?
x: Revealing identity is punishable with up to 3 years and ₹50,000; a false complaint with up to 2 years and ₹30,000.

s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, who is the competent authority for complaints against Central Government employees?
x: For Central employees the competent authority is the CVC; for Union Ministers it is the Prime Minister.

s: What did the Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2015 seek to do?
o: Bar disclosures in categories like those of RTI Section 8(1), such as security and Cabinet papers
Make the Lokpal the only competent authority
Extend the complaint limit to 10 years
x: The 2015 Bill, passed by the Lok Sabha in May 2015, would bar disclosures in RTI Section 8(1)-type categories; it lapsed in 2019.

s:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002:
I. The Act empowers authorities like the Director to attach property believed to be " proceeds of crime ".
II. Offences under Part A of the Schedule deal with trans-border crimes and reflect the dedication to tackle money laundering across the global boundaries.
III. The Act and the Rules notified thereunder came into force with effect from 2005.
IV. The Act has provided for an Appellate Tribunal and Special Court to conduct the trial of the offences of money laundering.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements I and III are supported by the notes: the ED Director can attach "proceeds of crime" under PMLA, and PMLA 2002 came into force on 1 July 2005. Statement IV (Appellate Tribunal and Special Court) is also part of the Act, so the answer is I, III and IV only. Statement II is the tempting wrong one: it is incorrect as framed, because Part A of the Schedule is not described as the trans-border crimes part.

s: What is the legal status of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)?
o: Non-constitutional, non-statutory body linked to the DSPE Act, 1946
Statutory body under the CVC Act, 2003
Judicial body under the Ministry of Law
x: The CBI is a non-constitutional, non-statutory body whose legal basis is linked to the DSPE Act, 1946.

s: What is the legal status of the Central Vigilance Commission?
o: Department of the Ministry of Finance under the PMLA
Independent statutory body established under the CVC Act, 2003
x: The CVC is an independent statutory body established under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

s: Which body exercises superintendence over the CBI in corruption cases?
x: The CVC supervises the CBI in corruption cases; the CBI rests on the DSPE Act, 1946, and the ED on the PMLA and FEMA.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Vigilance Commission?
o: It is a statutory body under the CVC Act 2003
It has superintendence over the CBI in corruption cases
It has up to 2 Vigilance Commissioners
Its members hold office for 5 years or until 65
x: CVC members hold office for 4 years or until 65, not 5 years; the other statements are correct.

s: The Enforcement Directorate functions under which ministry?
x: The ED works under the Ministry of Finance, the CBI under the Ministry of Personnel.

s: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, who can attach 'proceeds of crime'?
x: The ED Director can attach proceeds of crime under the PMLA.

s: Under which ministry does the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) function?
o: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
x: The CBI, based on the DSPE Act 1946, works under the Ministry of Personnel.

s: According to the CVC report of September 2026, what was the CBI's conviction rate in 2025?
x: The CVC report put the CBI's conviction rate at 71.71% in 2025, with 7,229 cases pending.

s: In the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta framework, the Lokayukta primarily deals with:
o: International relations, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with public order
Only judicial officers, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with private citizens
Higher functionaries, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the rest
Only Group C and D employees, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with Ministers
x: The Lokayukta has jurisdiction over higher functionaries, whereas the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the remaining categories covered by the state law.

s: Within what period did the 2013 central law on Lokpal and Lokayuktas require every State to set up a Lokayukta?
x: The 2013 Act obliged every State to establish a Lokayukta within one year of its commencement; States then framed widely differing laws. Six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.

s: Who was the first Lokpal of India?
x: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal in March 2019; Justice A.M. Khanwilkar became chairperson in February 2024.

s: Besides the Chairperson, the Lokpal under the 2013 Act may have up to how many members?
x: The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to 8 members, 50% of them judicial.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Lokpal selection committee?
x: The committee is the PM (chair), Speaker, LoP, CJI or a nominated SC judge and an eminent jurist; the Cabinet Secretary is not on it.

s: In which year was the AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, under which Andhra Pradesh's Lokayukta is established, enacted?
x: The AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act dates from 1983; the Lokayukta deals with higher functionaries.

s: Under the 2024 amendment, who chairs the selection committee that recommends the AP Lokayukta?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Since the 2024 amendment, a retired HC Chief Justice or Judge is appointed on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the CM, for 5 years.

s: Who became the chairperson of the Lokpal in February 2024?
x: Justice A.M. Khanwilkar became Lokpal chairperson in February 2024; the first Lokpal was Justice P.C. Ghose (2019).

s: Who was sworn in as the Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh on 25 August 2026?
x: Justice T. Mallikarjuna Rao took oath as AP Lokayukta before Governor S. Abdul Nazeer on 25 August 2026.

s: What share of the members of the Lokpal must be judicial members?
x: Under the 2013 Act, 50% of Lokpal members must be judicial members.

s: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, at least half of the Lokpal members must come from which groups?
o: SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women
x: At least 50% of Lokpal members must be from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women; 50% must be judicial.

s: Under the 2024 amendment, what is the term of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta?
x: The 2024 amendment made a retired HC Chief Justice or Judge the Lokayukta, chosen by a CM-led committee, for 5 years.

s: Under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, when may the Special Court confiscate a fugitive's property on the ED's application?
o: Only after a Supreme Court order
x: On the ED's application, the Special Court may confiscate property even before conviction.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 — Proceedings involving flight from India and confiscation by a Special Court
Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 — Attachment and confiscation of proceeds of corruption
Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 — Ban on proxy holdings
Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 — Imprisonment up to ten years as its stated maximum punishment
x: The Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 provides for confiscation and imprisonment up to seven years, not ten years. The other pairings are correctly stated.

s: Under the Benami Transactions (Amendment) Act, 2016, up to how many years of rigorous imprisonment is benami holding punishable?
x: The Benami Act provides confiscation and up to 7 years' rigorous imprisonment, not ten.

s: What is the minimum value of the offence for the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 to apply?
x: The FEOA applies where there is a warrant, an offence of ₹100 crore or more, and flight from India.

src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
s: According to Transparency International, the rank of India in the Corruption Perceptions Index, 2016 is
Who publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
x: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by Transparency International, headquartered in Berlin.

s: On the Corruption Perceptions Index scale of 0 to 100, what does a score of 0 denote?
x: The CPI measures perceived public-sector corruption on a 0-100 scale, where 0 denotes highly corrupt conditions.

s: What was India's rank in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025?
x: In CPI 2025 India ranked 91st of 182 with a score of 39; in 2024 it was 96th with 38.

s: What does the Corruption Perceptions Index measure?
x: The CPI of Transparency International measures perceived public-sector corruption from expert and business surveys.

s: Where is Transparency International, which publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index, headquartered?
x: Transparency International is based in Berlin and has published the CPI every year since 1995.

s: Since which year has Transparency International published the Corruption Perceptions Index?
x: Transparency International (Berlin) has published the CPI every year since 1995.

s: What was India's score in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025?
x: In CPI 2025 India scored 39 and ranked 91st of 182 (38 and 96th in 2024).

s: Who pioneered Citizen Report Cards in Bengaluru in the 1990s?
o: Central Vigilance Commission associated with K. Santhanam
Public Affairs Centre associated with Samuel Paul
Planning Commission associated with B. R. Ambedkar
Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan associated with Aruna Roy
x: Citizen Report Cards were developed by the Public Affairs Centre in Bengaluru in the 1990s under the leadership of Samuel Paul.

s: With which of the following is Jan Sunwai, as a method of citizen oversight, most closely associated?
o: Lokpal inquiries in Maharashtra during the 2000s
CVC hearings in Delhi during the 1980s
MKSS public hearings in Rajasthan during the 1990s
SSAAT audits in Andhra Pradesh during the 1970s
x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings associated with the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan in Rajasthan during the 1990s.

s: Which of the following pairs (citizen oversight tool – origin) is correctly matched?
o: Jan Sunwai – Public Affairs Centre, Bengaluru
Social audit – Gram Sabha audit of MGNREGA works
x: Social audit is the Gram Sabha's audit of scheme works; Citizen Report Cards come from the Public Affairs Centre and Jan Sunwai from MKSS.
